h1: The 6 Best Handheld Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six cordless handheld vacuums compared on filtration, attachments, pet-hair tools and charging.
summary: The DEWALT 20V handheld is the best handheld vacuum, with named HEPA filtration, six attachments and an LED light. The Shark WANDVAC is the compact pick that charges on a wall mount, and the BLACK+DECKER Dustbuster 20V adds an extendible crevice tool. The Shark Cyclone PET and Bissell Pet Hair Eraser cover pet owners, while the Dustbuster AdvancedClean is the budget entry.
intro: A handheld vacuum is bought for the spill, and it fails because of the weeks before the spill. The usual pattern is a full charge in January, a drawer in February, and a dead battery in March when the cereal hits the floor. For that reason, where the vacuum lives and how it charges matter more than any suction claim, and no listing here backs suction with a measured figure.

We reviewed six cordless handhelds and scored them on the Primea framework, weighing filtration, attachments, charging and storage, pet-hair design and the stated power platform. Runtime is unlisted across the group, so we say so rather than pretend to compare it. A vacuum that sits visible on a wall mount gets used far more often than a better one in a cabinet.

products.name: DEWALT 20V Handheld Vacuum Cordless, Car Vacuum with HEPA Filter, 6 Attachments and LED Light
products.verdict: HEPA filtration, six attachments and a light for dark corners.
products.description:
The DEWALT runs on the 20V platform and is pitched for cars as well as the home. It lists a named HEPA filter, six attachments and a built-in LED light, in the $100 to $200 tier. A HEPA filter traps fine particles instead of blowing them back into the room, which matters for allergies and for the dust a car stirs up. The light finds crumbs under seats.

It takes first place because no other listing offers filtration and attachments together, which makes it a complete tool and not a single-job gadget. The Shark WANDVAC beats it for storage, but not for capability.

Buy it for a car owner or an allergy-conscious household. The caveats are price, the highest among handhelds, and weight, so skip it if you only clean small kitchen spills.
products.skipIf: You only clean small kitchen spills.

products.name: Shark WANDVAC Cordless Hand Vac, Black, WV201BK
products.verdict: A small cordless vac that charges on the wall.
products.description:
The WANDVAC is a compact cordless hand vac from Shark with wall-mount charging, in the $50 to $100 tier. That mount is the practical feature: the vacuum sits on display, charged and within reach, so you grab it the moment something spills. It is the best answer to the drawer problem.

It slots behind the DEWALT because the listing names no HEPA filter or extra attachments. Where it wins is convenience, and it costs about half as much. Against the Dustbuster 20V, it gives up the extendible tool for easier storage.

Buy it for quick daily cleanups at home. The caveat is the thin accessory list, so skip it if you need detailing attachments for a car interior or upholstery, where the DEWALT or Dustbuster cover more ground.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Dustbuster 20V Hand Vacuum Cordless Rechargeable with Extendible Crevice Tool
products.verdict: A named 20V rating with a crevice tool that stretches.
products.description:
This Dustbuster states 20V power and includes an extendible crevice tool plus a flip-up brush, in the $50 to $100 tier. Those two tools cover tight corners and upholstery without extra purchases. An extendible crevice tool reaches the gap between a car seat and console, where a fixed nozzle cannot go.

It ranks third because it has fewer attachments than the DEWALT and no wall mount like the Shark. Its strength is the stated 20V rating, which tells you what battery platform you are buying, something several rivals leave vague.

Buy it for sofas, stairs and cars. The caveats are no named HEPA filter and no wall mount, so skip it if you want filtration or want a vacuum that charges where you can see it.

products.name: Shark Cyclone PET Handheld Vacuum, Navy Blue/Grey, CH701
products.verdict: Cyclone technology aimed at pet-hair cleanup.
products.description:
The Shark Cyclone PET is a pet-focused handheld with named cyclone technology, in the $50 to $100 tier. The cyclone design separates debris from the airflow, which is the idea behind keeping suction steady as the bin fills. Pet hair clogs plain filters quickly, so the design matters.

It ranks fourth because it is a specialist: the listing says little about accessories, and general cleaning gets less support than the DEWALT or Dustbuster provide. It edges the Bissell because cyclone separation is a documented mechanism.

Buy it for homes with shedding pets. The caveat is narrow focus and few listed accessories. Skip it if you need versatile attachments for cars and furniture, where a general model such as the DEWALT or Dustbuster is the better tool.

products.name: Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Cordless Hand Vacuum, Home, Auto & Pet, 2390A
products.verdict: Bissell's pet line for the home, the car and the dog bed.
products.description:
The Bissell Pet Hair Eraser carries Bissell's named pet technology and is pitched for home, auto and pet use, in the $50 to $100 tier. Its appeal is breadth: the same unit cleans the dog bed, the couch and the back seat, which suits owners who chase fur everywhere.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives few concrete specs beyond the brand's pet focus, so it is harder to compare with the Shark. Without a stated platform or filter, you take the maker's word on performance.

Buy it if you trust Bissell's pet line and clean the car too. The caveat is the sparse specification, with no HEPA named. Skip it if you want listed specs to compare, where the DEWALT and Dustbuster 20V document more.
products.idealFor: Pet owners who also clean the car.
products.skipIf: You want listed specs to compare.

products.name: Black+Decker Dustbuster AdvancedClean Handheld Vacuum Cordless, Compact Home and Car Vacuum with Crevice Tool
products.verdict: The cheapest way into a cordless hand vac with a charging base.
products.description:
The AdvancedClean includes a crevice tool, a rotating nozzle and a charging station, aimed at home and car cleanups, in the under $50 tier. The charging station is a hidden strength: like the WANDVAC's mount, it keeps the vacuum charged and parked in one place.

It finishes last because the listing names no power rating or filter, but the accessories and the price make it the easy entry point. Against the WANDVAC, it costs less and adds a rotating nozzle.

Buy it for a first handheld or a spare for the car. The caveat is the missing power rating and filter detail, so skip it if you want filtration or pet-hair tools. It is a basic tool for light jobs, not a replacement for a stronger model.
products.skipIf: You want filtration or pet tools.

whatMatters.detail: Filtration describes what happens to the dust after it enters the vacuum. A HEPA filter captures very small particles instead of blowing them back out, which matters for allergies and fine dust. Look for HEPA in the title, and note that most listings here omit it, so a standard filter is the default assumption. Washable filters save money over time.

Attachments decide how many jobs the vacuum can do. A crevice tool reaches corners and seat gaps, and a brush lifts dust and hair from fabric. Check how many pieces are included, since the DEWALT lists six and some rivals list one or two, and ask whether you will actually carry them around. Extra tools that stay in a drawer are wasted money.

Charging and storage decide whether you reach for the vacuum. A handheld that is charged and visible gets used more, so wall mounts and charging bases help. Look for wall-mount or charging station in the listing, as on the WANDVAC and AdvancedClean, and keep the dock where spills happen. A vacuum stored in the garage never helps the kitchen.

Pet-hair design adds brushes or cyclone systems to handle fur, which clogs ordinary filters fast. They help if your pet sheds heavily. Check for named pet technology in the title, such as the Cyclone PET or Pet Hair Eraser, and consider whether the bin is easy to empty. Fur packs tightly, so a wide opening saves time.

A stated voltage like 20V tells you the battery platform, which helps compare power across brands and may let you share batteries with tools. Check the title for the voltage, and be cautious when a listing omits it, as several here do, because you cannot judge the power class. Voltage alone does not guarantee suction, but silence is worse.

faq.q: How long does a handheld vacuum battery last?
faq.a: Listings rarely publish runtime in comparable terms. Plan for short cleanups, charge it after each use, and favor a model with a wall mount or base, like the WANDVAC or AdvancedClean. A vacuum that is always charged is one that gets used.

It matters for allergies or fine dust, such as in a car or a bedroom. For crumbs and dirt, a standard filter is fine. Only the DEWALT names HEPA in this group, so allergy sufferers have one clear pick.

faq.q: Is the DEWALT worth it over the Shark?
faq.a: If you need filtration and attachments, yes. For quick kitchen use the Shark WANDVAC is easier, since it charges on the wall and is always ready.

faq.q: How do I clean the filter?
faq.a: Empty the bin, tap the filter clean and rinse only if the manual allows. Let it dry fully before putting it back, especially on the Shark and Bissell pet models, where fur and damp can mat.

faq.q: How do I keep the battery healthy?
faq.a: Store it on its charger or at partial charge, and avoid leaving it in a hot car, since heat shortens battery life. The DEWALT and Dustbuster 20V use rechargeable batteries that dislike heat.

faq.q: Can a handheld replace my main vacuum?
faq.a: No. It handles small areas and spills, not whole floors. The DEWALT is the strongest handheld here, but a full-size vacuum still does the main job. Use the handheld for the gaps.

finalTake: Buy the DEWALT if you want filtration and a full tool set, especially for a car. The WANDVAC is the better choice for quick kitchen cleanups, since it lives on the wall and is always charged. Pet owners should look at the Shark Cyclone PET or Bissell, and the AdvancedClean is the cheap way to find out whether you use a handheld at all. None replaces a main vacuum.
